//: Per-zone client-bundle ceilings in gzipped KB, measured in two halves from Vite's manifest. `staticGzipKB` is the closure of STATIC imports from every emitted entry (entry/start, entry/app and every route node) plus their CSS — what crossing into the zone actually costs. `deferredGzipKB` is everything reachable only through a dynamic import — real bytes, but ones the user opts into. The split exists because one number could not tell those apart: the annotator once measured 4179 KB of which 3809 was OpenCV wasm behind a lazy import, so a doubling of its entry graph would have passed unnoticed. That blob is gone (#117 — two ops reimplemented in @rask/engine/tools/corners.ts), which is why the annotator's deferred ceiling is now in line with every other zone's. Raise a number ONLY with the reason in the commit message; that edit is the review.

home.note: The landing + the OIDC round-trip. Should stay the smallest thing in the estate; if it grows, something that belongs in a domain zone has leaked into the shell. Measured 157 / 1.

lakehouse.note: Four areas (catalog, lineage, models, admin) in one router, plus this zone's OWN dock at /lakehouse/workbench (lineage graph + runs + events over ONE LineageState, and the catalog's real TableRegistry + ObjectBrowser). Carries @xyflow/svelte for the lineage graph and layerchart for the model experiments. 2026-08-04: deferred 120 -> 160. @rask/dockview is ~67 KB gz behind a dynamic import on that ONE route, which is exactly where dock invariant 4 wants it — but it took the measured deferred half to 119 of 120, one kilobyte of headroom, so the gate would next fire on rounding rather than on a regression. 160 keeps it failing on a doubling. Measured 545 / 119.

explorer.note: embedding-atlas + d3 + elkjs for the atlas/tree/graph surfaces, plus this zone's dock at /explorer/workbench (results + atlas + player over one Bench store). The HEAVIEST zone to enter. 2026-08-04: deferred 120 -> 160, same reason as lakehouse — the dock is ~66 KB gz behind a dynamic import (invariant 4) and left only 1 KB of headroom at 119 of 120. Measured 961 / 119.

annotator.note: Pixi ships in the entry graph (a canvas is the whole point of the zone) and is most of the cost. The deferred ceiling was 4200 while the magnetic tool pulled a vendored OpenCV build; #117 replaced its two calls (cvtColor RGBA->GRAY, cornerMinEigenVal) with ~120 lines in @rask/engine/tools/corners.ts, pinned to OpenCV's recorded output, and the deferred half fell 3854 -> 46 KB with the entry graph unchanged. 2026-08-04: static 420 -> 460. The entry graph grew 365 -> 420 with the project-ontology work (LabelOntology replacing the schema/template pair, and the model registry surface). It then landed EXACTLY on the old ceiling and FLAPPED — 421 on one build, 420 on the next — so the gate reddened CI at random instead of reporting anything. The 55 KB is recorded here rather than absorbed silently: if that surface should be lazy, this note is where to start. Measured 420 / 46.

compute.note: The Ray surfaces (cluster, jobs, actors, serve, logviewer) over the shared shell — tables and status views, no heavy vendored runtime, so the ENTRY cost should stay near the home zone's weight. The deferred ceiling is 110: this zone now ships its OWN dock at /compute/workbench (jobs + capacity + actors + serve over the zone's remotes), and @rask/dockview is ~67 KB gz behind a dynamic import on that ONE route of eleven — measured 74 total. Nothing else in this zone is lazy, so the dock IS the deferred half; 110 still fails on a doubling.

studio.note: The studio zone; gsap rides in the entry graph for the animation surface and is the only dependency beyond the shared shell, so this should stay light. Measured 163 / 1.

train.note: The train zone (R17): five dummy areas — submit form, run board, monitoring, analysis, model registry — over the shared shell, no dependency beyond it, so it should stay near studio's weight until real training surfaces land. Measured 184 / 1.
